# RAM vs. Storage

## RAM (Random Access Memory)
- **Purpose**: Temporary working memory your computer uses for active tasks
- **Speed**: Very fast
- **Volatility**: Data is erased when power is off
- **Typical size**: 8–64 GB
- **Analogy**: Your desk — space to spread out what you're currently working on

## Storage (SSD/HDD)
- **Purpose**: Long-term holding of files, apps, and the operating system
- **Speed**: Slower than RAM (though SSDs are quite fast)
- **Volatility**: Data persists even when powered off
- **Typical size**: 256 GB – several TB
- **Analogy**: Your filing cabinet — where everything is kept permanently

## How They Work Together
When you open an app or file, it's copied from storage into RAM so the CPU can access it quickly. More RAM lets you run more things simultaneously without slowdown; more storage lets you keep more files and programs installed.

**Quick example**: A photo lives on your storage drive permanently, but when you're editing it, the photo and editing software are loaded into RAM for fast access.
